questions.question: Which of the following is a dance form in Mizoram participated exclusively by 'village guests'?
questions.solution:
Khuallam, literally meaning 'Dance of the Guests', is a traditional folk dance of Mizoram. It is performed during the ceremony of Khuangchawi, where guests entering the village from other hamlets participate in the dance.

Note: Dancers wear the traditional hand-woven Mizo cloth known as Puandum.

questions.question: With which of the following classical dances is ‘Kottakkal Sivaraman’ associated?
questions.solution: Kottakkal Sivaraman was a legendary performer of Kathakali, specializing in Streevesham (female roles). He is credited with bringing a new level of psychological depth and emotional expression to the female characters in this Kerala dance-drama.

questions.question: ‘Ranapa’, a folk dance form of Odisha, consists of enacting chapters from the life of Lord ______.
questions.solution: Ranapa is a energetic folk dance of Odisha, particularly popular in the Ganjam district. The dancers perform on stilts (Ranapa) and enact stories from the childhood and life of Lord Krishna.

questions.question: To which of the following states does the dance drama ‘Khyal’ belong?
questions.solution:
Khyal (or Khayal) is a traditional dance-drama form belonging to Rajasthan. It involves the narration of mythological or historical stories through song and dance.

Note: It is distinct from the Khayal genre of Hindustani classical music.

questions.question: Which of the following is a dance form of West Bengal where there is a confluence of dancing, singing, drama and recital?
questions.solution: Alkap is a rural performance art popular in West Bengal (especially Murshidabad and Malda) and parts of Jharkhand. It is a seamless blend of dance, song, drama, and rhythmic recital, usually performed by a troupe of 10 to 12 members.

questions.question: 'Maimata' is a popular dance of the Kaloi community from the state of ______.
questions.solution: Maimata is a popular folk dance of the Kaloi community in Tripura. It is usually performed during harvest festivals to express gratitude to the deities for a bountiful crop.

questions.question: Kalbelia folk songs and dance forms are an expression of the Kalbelia community’s traditional way of life. It is associated with which of the following states?
questions.solution:
Kalbelia is an iconic folk dance of Rajasthan, performed by the tribe of the same name. The movements are highly flexible and mimic the slithering of a snake, which is why it is often called the 'Snake Charmer Dance'.

Status: It is recognized by UNESCO as Intangible Cultural Heritage.

questions.question: 'Bhand Pather' is a form of theatre dance performed in ______.
questions.solution: Bhand Pather is a traditional folk theatre form of Kashmir. It combines satire, farcical elements, and music. The word 'Bhand' refers to the traditional entertainers, and 'Pather' means drama.

questions.question: With which of the following musical instruments is the musician Zakir Hussain associated?
questions.solution: Ustad Zakir Hussain is a world-renowned maestro of the Tabla. A child prodigy and son of Ustad Alla Rakha, he has been a global ambassador for Indian percussion and was awarded the Padma Vibhushan in 2023.

questions.question: With which of the following musical instruments was the musician Bismillah Khan associated?
questions.solution:
Ustad Bismillah Khan was the legendary musician who single-handedly brought the Shehnai (a wind instrument) to the center stage of Indian classical music.

Honor: He was awarded India's highest civilian award, the Bharat Ratna, in 2001.

questions.question: With which of the following states is the traditional instrument called 'Pena' associated?
questions.solution: The Pena is an ancient stringed musical instrument associated with the state of Manipur. It is a mono-string instrument used primarily in folk music and during the Lai Haraoba festival.

questions.question: Pt. Satish Vyas was conferred upon the prestigious Tansen Samman in December 2020. He was associated with which of the following musical instruments?
questions.solution: Pandit Satish Vyas is an eminent Santoor player and a disciple of the legendary Pt. Shiv Kumar Sharma. He was honored with the Tansen Samman in 2020 by the Madhya Pradesh government for his contribution to music.

questions.question: Which of the following musical instruments is an example of the stringed instruments played by the Manganiars of west Rajasthan?
questions.solution: The Kamaicha is a unique bowed string instrument used by the Manganiar folk musicians of Western Rajasthan. It is carved out of a single piece of mango wood and has a large circular resonator covered with goatskin.

questions.question: The musical instrument 'Kartal' from the state of Rajasthan comes under the category of ______.
questions.solution: The Kartal is a percussion instrument from Rajasthan that falls under the category of Idiophones. Idiophones are instruments that create sound through the vibration of the instrument's entire body without the use of strings or membranes.

questions.question: With which of the following musical instruments is the musician Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma associated?
questions.solution:
Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma was the pioneer who elevated the Santoor from a Kashmiri folk instrument to a world-renowned classical instrument.

Note: He collaborated with flautist Pt. Hariprasad Chaurasia for several iconic film scores under the name Shiv-Hari.

questions.question: Which of the following festivals of Tamil Nadu is dedicated to Lord Muruga?
questions.solution: Thai Poosam is a major festival in Tamil Nadu dedicated to Lord Muruga (the son of Shiva and Parvati). It commemorates the occasion when Muruga received a 'Vel' (spear) to vanquish the demon Soorapadman.

questions.question: Which of the following is an animal trading festival of Gujarat?
questions.solution: The Vautha Mela is a famous animal trading fair (specifically for donkeys and camels) held at the confluence of seven rivers in Gujarat. It is considered one of the largest such fairs in India, second only to the Sonepur Mela in Bihar.

questions.question: 'Ali Ai Ligang Festival' is a festival celebrated in the state of ______.
questions.solution: Ali Ai Ligang is a vibrant spring festival celebrated by the Mising tribe of Assam. The name refers to the start of the seed-sowing season ('Ali' means seeds, 'Ai' means fruit, and 'Ligang' means sowing).

questions.question: Teeyan is a festival celebrated in Punjab, which celebrates the onset of ______.
questions.solution: Teeyan is the Punjabi name for the festival of Teej, which celebrates the onset of the Monsoon. It is primarily a women's festival involving swings, traditional songs (Gidda), and dressing in vibrant clothes.

questions.question: ‘Sakewa’ is a religious festival celebrated in the state of ______.
questions.solution: Sakewa is a significant religious and agricultural festival celebrated by the Rai community in Sikkim. It involves prayers to Mother Earth for a good harvest and the performance of the Sili (dance).

questions.question: ‘Nuakhai’ is the greatest harvesting festival of Odisha, celebrated one day after of which of the following festivals?
questions.solution: Nuakhai, the harvest festival of Odisha, is celebrated one day after Ganesh Chaturthi. It involves the ritual of eating the 'new rice' harvested from the fields.

questions.question: Which of the following festivals is celebrated as a kite-flying festival across India?
questions.solution: Makar Sankranti is celebrated across India as a kite-flying festival (known as Uttarayan in Gujarat). It marks the transition of the sun into the zodiac sign of Capricorn and the start of warmer days.

questions.question: In which festival of Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh, are the bullocks and other cattles used for agriculture worshipped?
questions.solution: The Pola festival is celebrated in Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh by farmers to worship bullocks and oxen. It is a gesture of gratitude for the animals' hard work in the agricultural fields throughout the year.

questions.question: In which of the following states is the Losoong festival celebrated?
questions.solution: Losoong (or Namsoong) is the Sikkimese New Year festival, celebrated by the Bhutia and Lepcha tribes in Sikkim. It marks the end of the harvest season and is famous for the Black Hat dance.

questions.question: 'Kati Bihu' in Assam is celebrated by lighting a lamp in front of a ______ tree / plant.
questions.solution: During Kati Bihu (or Kongali Bihu) in Assam, people light an earthen lamp (Saki) at the foot of the Tulsi (Holy Basil) plant. It is a solemn occasion where prayers are offered for the protection of the ripening paddy crops.
